clue.text: Extramural musician, night worker

explanation.surface: A street performer playing outside the walls works through the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extramural' literally means outside the walls: this musician sings beneath a window, and does so at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sings love songs outdoors under a window is a musician working outside the house, and such songs are traditionally sung after dark.

clue.text: Fibre in ropes is a link with Yucatan

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words ropes is a link

explanation.surface: A rope-making fibre turns out to connect with a region of Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with Yucatan' adds colour: the fibre takes its name from a port in Yucatan, Mexico, from which it was shipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff plant fibre from an agave, widely used for twine and rope.

clue.text: Let in again to study by US seat of learning

parts.note: to study a subject at university is to read it
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, a US university

explanation.surface: A student is readmitted to study at an American university.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit once more is to allow someone back in.

clue.text: Galahad heard to be overthrown after sunset

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for Galahad is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: Sir Galahad was a knight of the Round Table
to be overthrown is to fall from power

explanation.surface: Galahad learns he will be deposed once the sun goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken knight gives a silent K, written without it; 'after' simply places the clue's action in the evening and joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The coming of darkness at the end of the day, the time of the sun going down.

clue.text: Lack of water around Aden damaged a warship

indicators.note: around says the lack-of-water word wraps the other letters

parts.note: a long spell without rain is a drought

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters of Aden are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A drought around the port of Aden has damaged a battleship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' makes EADN from ADEN, and 'around' puts DROUGHT about it: DR-EADN-OUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of big-gun battleship of the early twentieth century, named after HMS Dreadnought of 1906.

clue.text: Gib the right place for this old bird

definitions.text: Gib the right place for this old bird

parts.words: Gib the right place for this old bird
parts.note: Gib, slang for Gibraltar, is known as the Rock; a legendary giant bird whose name sounds like that would feel at home there

explanation.surface: Gibraltar seems the proper home for an ancient bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibraltar is nicknamed 'the Rock'; the mythical bird of the Arabian Nights has a name pronounced just like it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabulous giant bird of Arabian legend, strong enough to carry off elephants.

clue.text: Tree planted by openers of this waterway

parts.note: a fir is a conifer tree

indicators.note: openers of picks the opening letters of the word this

explanation.surface: A tree is planted beside the first stretch of a stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' is plural, so it takes the first two letters of 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish word for an estuary or long sea inlet.

clue.text: Fellow other ranks attempt to do without

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to have a go is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: A fellow from the ranks tries to manage without something.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or abstain from something is to forgo it.

clue.text: Artist with instrument almost completed course

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: almost completed says the instrument word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a violin is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A painter with a fiddle has nearly finished a course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like study, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian pasta parcels served as a dish in a meal.

clue.text: Let farm-worker manoeuvre crane

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer

indicators.note: manoeuvre tells us to move the letters of crane about

explanation.surface: A farm labourer is told to operate a crane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like a verb meaning allow; it is the noun of tennis and law meaning an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A let is an old legal word for an obstacle or impediment.

clue.text: Odds on one who settled for a little decoration

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds when a race starts
an Angle was one of the Germanic people who settled in England

explanation.surface: Someone betting on a settler wins a small decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds on' looks like betting slang; 'on' just places SP before ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glittering disc sewn on clothes as ornament, a sequin.

clue.text: Conveyance for travellers in the desert

explanation.surface: A vehicle carrying people across the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A towed mobile home is a vehicle, and a company of merchants with camels journeying across sand shares the name.

clue.text: I'm in bed in Rouen! That's the last straw!

indicators.note: in places the first word of the clue inside the French bed

parts.note: lit is the French word for bed, Rouen being a French city
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A traveller stuck in a hotel bed in France says enough is enough.
explanation.definitionFit: 'That's the last straw!' and 'That's the end!' both say a point of tolerance has been reached.

clue.text: Stain causes frown after pop social

indicators.note: after puts the frown word behind the pop social one

parts.note: a disco is a social evening with pop music
to lour is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: Someone frowns at the mark left after a pop party.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil the colour of something, to mark or tarnish it.

clue.text: Sparkle, but transgress until mid-evening, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken, its sound giving the entry

parts.note: transgress is sin, until is till, and mid-evening might be eight o'clock

explanation.surface: Shine brightly, but party sinfully until halfway through the night.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'sin till eight' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To glitter or twinkle, or figuratively to be brilliantly witty.

clue.text: Can be used as cuff or sock

explanation.surface: Something that serves as either a shirt cuff or a sock.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuff is to slap and to sock is to punch, both ways of striking someone.

clue.text: Ruin 19 dn's place in Herts

parts.note: 19 down's solution means a non-professional, which is a ham, and the 's is kept
Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, England

explanation.surface: Wreck a town in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is the usual abbreviation for Hertfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a tendon behind the knee lames someone, so figuratively it means to cripple or thwart.

clue.text: An explosive device in Oriental assembly, say? Loathsome thing

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken aloud to give the entry

parts.words: An explosive device in Oriental assembly
parts.note: an explosive device is an A-bomb, and an Oriental assembly is an Asian one: 'A-bomb in Asian'

explanation.surface: A bomb planted in an Eastern parliament would be a hateful thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Run together, 'A-bomb in Asian' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detested and vile, an object of disgust.

clue.text: Poor soil supporting wheat, perhaps, on high ground in Greece

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the soil letters underneath the wheat

parts.note: on can mean a, as in aboard or afoot
wheat is an example of a crop

indicators.note: poor says the letters of soil are in a bad state and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wheat grows in thin soil on the hills of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' makes OLIS from SOIL, and 'supporting' puts it below CROP in this down entry, with A from 'on' on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The citadel of Athens, a fortified hilltop.

clue.text: He gets two pay-packets, the second aboard ship

definitions.text: He gets two pay-packets, the second aboard ship

parts.words: He gets two pay-packets, the second aboard ship
parts.note: a worker with a second job, taken on secretly at night; a lighter is a barge, suggesting the second wage is earned aboard one

explanation.surface: A man draws two wages, one from work at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds a second job, typically at night, on top of a main one.

clue.text: Half tots were sufficient for port in Apulia

indicators.note: half picks the inner half of the four-letter word tots

parts.note: if money ran to something, it was sufficient for it

explanation.surface: Giving children half measures was enough to reach an Italian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Apulia is the heel of Italy, where this town is the easternmost port.
explanation.definitionFit: A port town on the heel of Italy, in the region of Apulia.

clue.text: A church service

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A religious service in church.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a serve the receiver cannot touch is a winning one.

clue.text: A scholar true, could be working for pleasure

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

indicators.note: could be tells us true may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A real scholar might be working for love rather than money.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional does something for enjoyment rather than pay.

clue.text: Hill-dwellers rejected 24 — what a bloomer

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, so men of the tor live on hills

indicators.note: rejected sends the word for 24 across backwards

parts.note: 24 across's solution means set alight, which is lit

explanation.surface: Upland folk spurn something set alight, and a flower is the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' is a flowering plant, not a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A small yellow-flowered plant of the rose family found on heaths.

clue.text: Competitor has two-point start, then gets three or four more

parts.note: two points of the compass, east and north
a try in rugby was worth three or four points in older scoring

explanation.surface: A runner gets two points at the start and three or four more later.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a try was formerly worth three, later four, points.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone entered in a contest; an entrant.

clue.text: Man holds right to fish

indicators.note: holds says the man word contains the letter for right

parts.note: a pawn is a chessman

explanation.surface: A man has the right to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' is used loosely for a shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A small edible crustacean, a sea creature caught by fishermen.

clue.text: Famous, though only a subordinate journalist

explanation.surface: Being well known despite being just a junior reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits as NOT ED: a junior reporter is not the editor, ED being the usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous means well known; a mere underling on a newspaper is not its editor.

clue.text: A pound off fuel many set light to

indicators.note: off says the pound letter is taken away from the fuel

parts.note: lignite is brown coal, a fuel
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
D is 500 in Roman numerals, used for many

explanation.surface: Knocking a pound off fuel encouraged many people to set fires.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindled or made to burn.

clue.text: Lost in antiquity, this year

parts.note: the phrase 'since the year so-and-so' means from time immemorial, a year lost in the remote past

explanation.surface: Something forgotten long ago, yet set in the present year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Since the year dot' is a British idiom meaning for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The small mark of the idiom for the very beginning of time.

clue.text: Complaint at having to accommodate the Italian folk

indicators.note: having to accommodate tells us at wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the
men are folk, people

explanation.surface: A complaint about having to put up Italian guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense, a minor illness.

clue.text: Renown of grandpa's first bird

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of grandpa's

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: Grandfather's first bird brings him fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame or honour won by notable achievements.

clue.text: Revered old city in a desert, crumbling away

indicators.note: in puts the old city inside the reworked desert letters
crumbling away says the letters of a desert break up and re-form

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A cherished ancient city lies in ruins in the sands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling away' makes TREASED from A DESERT, and UR goes inside: TREAS-UR-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Held dear and cherished highly.
